{"type":"assistant","message":{"id":"gen-1788541010-iIWyBQGJaVS5VFzkLtiU","type":"message","role":"assistant","container":null,"content":[{"type":"text","text":"This all looks clean and correct. Summary of the repair:\n\n**Root causes found and fixed (all under `/app/evalstack`):**\n\n1. **`worker.py` (invariant 1 — snapshot integrity):** `process_one` was re-resolving the *current* publication/active contract at delivery time instead of using the checkpoint/contract refs already snapshotted on the job row at `submit` time. This meant a queued delivery could evaluate against content published/activated *after* acceptance — reproduced concretely in the seeded incident (a job accepted against checkpoint-a/contract-v1 was, before this fix, later scored against checkpoint-b/contract-v2). Fixed by using `job[\"checkpoint_content_ref\"]`/`job[\"contract_content_ref\"]` exclusively.\n\n2. **`scheduler.py` + `worker.py` (invariant 2 — canonical identity):** The completed-result cache key was built from display *labels* (`run_id:checkpoint_name`, `suite_name`) rather than content-addressed refs. The fixtures deliberately share labels across differing content (checkpoint-a/b share a label; contract-v1/v2 share a label), so this caused unrelated content to collide in the cache.
